# Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more!

Day 2, 13:30 · Gary Illyes, Search Relations · coverage: transcript, one-slide

Short introduction to feature extraction (structured data, images, video). Introduced by name by the host and named again in the hand-over at the end of the next talk.

## Claims

- **[Slide]** Google's indexing pipeline slide put a Processing stage between the crawler and the index and listed HTML parsing, rendering, deduplication and feature extraction above it, with feature extraction highlighted as the step of this talk.
  <br><sub>`D2-C441` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C063](D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Repeats [D2-C026](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's indexing pipeline slide drew a feedback line from the Processing stage back to the crawl queue.
  <br><sub>`D2-C442` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Repeats [D2-C048](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's indexing includes a dedicated system, whose internal name Gary Illyes would not disclose, that extracts the parts of a page that are traditionally expensive to extract.
  <br><sub>`D2-C443` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google runs deduplication before feature extraction, so that the expensive extraction work is spent only on a trimmed-down, manageable set of documents.
  <br><sub>`D2-C444` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C026](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-10`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to how Search works says rendering happens during the crawl, and describes indexing as analysing a page's text, key tags and attributes such as title elements and alt attributes, images and videos, and deciding whether the page is a duplicate or the canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C445` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! · is the documentation · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Used by `DEV-HTM-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** The 'gold nuggets' that Google's feature extraction step pulls out of a page's HTML are structured data (such as JSON-LD), images and videos.
  <br><sub>`D2-C446` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works), [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Extended by [D3-C323](D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For images, Google's feature extraction takes the img element with its src and other attributes, including inline images, and passes them on to Google's image indexing service.
  <br><sub>`D2-C447` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Repeated by [D2-C524](D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For videos, Google's feature extraction takes the video itself and the data around it, to get a better sense of what happens in the video, and passes them to Google's media indexing engine.
  <br><sub>`D2-C448` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Video SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/video) · Extended by [D2-C930](D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) · Used by `DEV-VID-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said feature extraction, which extracts page structures into a form Google's systems can consume internally, is still expensive, though not the most expensive operation.
  <br><sub>`D2-C449` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Because Google extracts structured data, images and videos only after deduplication, put markup and media on the URL you want as canonical and keep them identical on its duplicates; markup that exists only on a duplicate that loses canonical selection may never be extracted.
  <br><sub>`D2-C450` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! · Used by `DEV-SDA-10`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's general structured data guidelines recommend placing the same structured data on all duplicate pages of the same content, not just on the canonical page.
  > "we recommend placing the same structured data on all page duplicates, not just on the canonical page"
  <br><sub>`D2-C451` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! · is the documentation · [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Used by `DEV-SDA-10`</sub>
